title: MVC, MVVM, VIPER, TCA, Clean: choosing an architecture
summary: All these patterns try to answer one question: where does each kind of code live so the app stays easy to change and test? There is no best one; choose by team size, complexity and testability needs.
body: **MVC (Apple's classic):** Model = data, View = UI, Controller = glue. In practice the view controller ends up doing everything ("Massive View Controller") and is hard to test.

**MVVM:** the View shows state from a **ViewModel**; the ViewModel holds screen state and logic, talks to services, and knows nothing about UIKit/SwiftUI views. Easy to unit test. Natural fit for SwiftUI + `@Observable`. Risk: huge view models - move business rules into services/use cases.
**MVVM-C:** MVVM + **Coordinator** that owns navigation, so view controllers do not push each other.

**VIPER / Clean Architecture:** strict layers - View, Interactor (business logic), Presenter (formatting), Entity (models), Router (navigation). Very clear boundaries for big UIKit teams, but a lot of files and boilerplate for small features.

**TCA / unidirectional (Redux-like):** one State, Actions, a Reducer that changes state, and Effects for side effects. Very predictable and testable. Costs: learning curve, third-party dependency, care needed for performance with big state.
**Real-life analogy:** a restaurant. MVC = one person cooks, serves and bills. MVVM = waiter (view) and kitchen (view model) are separate. VIPER = every job has its own specialist.

**Staff answer:** do not pick a brand name; standardize a few building blocks - state container, dependency injection, navigation, side-effect layer - write an ADR, provide templates and lint rules, and allow justified exceptions. Migrate gradually (strangler pattern), starting with the most-changed screens.
keyPoints: MVC is simple but leads to massive view controllers.
MVVM: testable view models with no UI imports; coordinators/routers for navigation.
TCA/unidirectional: single state + reducer, very testable, steeper learning.
Choose by team size and complexity; consistency across the codebase matters more than the pattern.

View models importing UIKit and holding references to views.
followups: **Where does business logic live?** In domain/use-case types independent of the UI framework, so it can be tested and reused.
**How would you migrate an MVC app?** Screen by screen: extract a view model and services from the most-changed controllers first; add tests as you go.
**Is MVVM needed with SwiftUI?** Not always; small views can keep `@State`. Use a model/view model when there is logic or async work worth testing.
